original_title: DOJ Sues Trump and Fred Trump for Racial Housing Discrimination (1973)

existing.title: DOJ Sues Trump and Fred Trump for Racial Housing Discrimination (1973)
existing.description_short: DOJ Sues Trump and Fred Trump for Racial Housing Discrimination (1973)

context.synopsis: In October 1973, the U.S. Department of Justice filed a landmark civil rights lawsuit against Donald Trump, his father Fred Trump, and their Trump Management Corporation, alleging systematic racial discrimination across 39 properties in New York. Black applicants were coded with a 'C' on their applications — standing for 'colored' — and steered away from vacancies. Undercover DOJ investigators confirmed the practice, finding that white applicants were offered apartments denied to Black applicants with equal or better qualifications. The case became one of the largest civil rights housing suits ever filed at the time. Trump publicly denied wrongdoing and counter-sued the DOJ for $100 million, a suit that was quickly dismissed.
context.recovered_rationale: This matters because federal investigators documented systematic racial discrimination in housing applications and confirmed that Black applicants were denied apartments offered to similarly qualified white applicants. The lawsuit therefore records institutionalized exclusion across numerous properties, supported by undercover findings, and shows that the conduct prompted a major federal civil rights enforcement action followed by an unsuccessful counter-suit.

sources.support_note: The litigation archive documents the 1973 DOJ case against Fred Trump, Donald Trump and Trump Management, including tester evidence, alleged racial coding of applications, the $100 million counterclaim, and the 1975 consent decree without an admission of liability.
sources.title: United States v. Fred C. Trump, Donald Trump, and Trump Management, Inc. 1:73-01529 (E.D.N.Y.)
